description: Decide what an arriving retry timer fire does. Creating a retry entry cancels any timer already armed for the issue, but cancellation is not synchronous, so a fire from the cancelled arming can still arrive. A fire dispatches only when its generation equals the current retry entry's; otherwise it is discarded and the entry and its armed timer are left in place. Testing only whether an entry is present is not sufficient, because a replaced entry is present.
given: { entry: { generation: integer, attempt: integer } | null, fire_generation: integer }

vectors.description: The live arming's fire. The entry is consumed and the issue is dispatched at the entry's attempt.

A cancelled timer fired anyway and its entry has since been replaced. The fire is discarded. entry_retained is the half a pop-then-test implementation fails: it removes the entry before it compares, so the live arming's backoff is consumed by a fire that did not belong to it.

A fire for an issue that has no retry entry. Discarded. Unreachable where timer fires are delivered in the order they were enqueued, and retained because SPEC.md states no delivery-ordering property for orchestrator messages, which is the same premise the generation non-reuse requirement rests on.
